topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture by connecting to histopathology practicals and setting out the core learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor virology, cellular oncogenes, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: They trace how the study of transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and establish the laboratory assays used to test cell transformation.

topics.label: Classes and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: They define functional categories of cancer mutations and illustrate how alterations in gene dosage and cell cycle regulators like Rb and p53 drive oncogenesis.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the cellular origins and phenotypic outcomes of sequence and chromosomal instability arising from defective DNA repair and mitotic errors.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how stepwise mutation accumulation drives tumor progression and how inherited germline mutations accelerate cancer development.

topics.label: Conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture, offers book recommendations, and previews the upcoming session.
